JUDGEMENT CALLS:
* S23 (728,444) - CROSSING. The x~707 diode column makes an unmistakable semicircular sideways jog (ink runs x=707 -> x=730 -> back to x=707 between y=425 and y=460) around the y~440 supply wire. Joining them would tie the diode string to the +6V/+5V rail and short out both diodes.
* S52 (605,769) - CROSSING (overrides the tracer's default junction). inkmap at (605,769) shows the R#15 column jogging from x=586 out to x=604 and back to x=587 across rows 756-780 while the y~769 horizontal runs straight through: a textbook hop. Reading it as a junction (the tracer's default) merged the whole n10 branch into the bottom rail, which put the collector AND the emitter of Q#20 on the same net (a dead short across the transistor) and left Q#19's base tied to its own emitter - electrically impossible. As a crossing, n10 = {Q#11 collector, Q#20 collector, Q#19 base} and the rail keeps 7 terminals.
* S21 (479,440) - JUNCTION. Plain 4-way X (+6V stem from above, R#8 from the left, R#9 to the right, Q#11 emitter below) with a modest blob (dot 2.1, the same score as the unambiguous Ts at S4/S8/S19) and NO jog. This drafter draws an explicit sideways jog when he means 'not connected' (twice on this sheet, S23 and S52), so a bare crossing here is a real junction. The crossing reading would instead give {+6V, Q#11 emitter} and {R#8, R#9 in series} - also electrically legal, which is why this is the one call on the sheet resting on the ink prior rather than on impossibility.
* S22 (815,442) - JUNCTION, and not a close call: a solid symmetric solder blob ~10x10 px against a 3 px stroke (dot 2.8).
* Every other CRITICAL site is a plain T (a wire ending on another wire) and was recorded as junction after looking at its 5x crop: S4 (+15V stem onto the top rail), S8 (+10V wire onto the R#1/R#4 column), S19 (R#8 onto the R#4/Q#10 column), S20 (+5V stem onto the y~438 wire), S40 (+3V column to Q#14 base), S41 (Q#16 collector onto the x~815 column), S42 (dotted node feeding Q#16 base off the diode column), S43 (Q#20 collector onto the Q#11-collector wire), S58/S59/S60/S61/S62 (the five risers landing on the bottom rail).

PORT / PIN FIXES:
* #7 (+5V): terminal 0 was pointing at the '+' stroke of the '+5V' text at (930,395), leaving the source on a one-terminal net. Repointed to p1 (900,432), the arrow stem that meets the y~438 wire at S20.
* #10 and #11 (BJT-PNP): both are drawn with the emitter on top - the emitter arrowhead points INTO the base bar on the upper lead in both cases (verified at 9x). The tracer's geometric default made the upper lead t0, i.e. it reported emitter,base,collector. Swapped to collector,base,emitter: #10 t0=p0(264,571 bottom), t1=p1(224,515 base), t2=p2(266,465 top); #11 t0=p0(486,588 bottom), t1=p2(522,540 base, right), t2=p1(482,486 top).
* #21 (BJT-NPN): drawn with the base bar at x~807 and the base lead leaving it to the LEFT at y~848, collector up-right to (822,813), emitter down-right (arrow) to (819,894). The tracer picked the top lead as the odd one. Corrected to t0=p0 (top, collector), t1=p2 (785,812, base), t2=p1 (bottom, emitter).
* #18 (BJT-NPN): drawn mirrored - base bar at x~282 with the base lead going RIGHT (295,784, the long wire to Q#20's base), collector up-left to (250,745), emitter down-left with the arrowhead to (256,820). t1 and t2 were therefore repointed to p1 and p0. The collector has no port candidate at all: the tracer swallowed the wire tip at (251,722) into site S44 (a 1-px stub at (248,726)) 3 px above the top edge of #18's box, so it never became a port. The ink is unambiguous at 8x - the x~250 column from Q#10's collector bends at (250,745) straight into #18's collector lead - so terminal 0 is set explicitly with manual_nets to n8, the Q#10 collector net. This is the only place on the sheet where a connection is asserted rather than traced.

No class corrections: all 9 BJTs, 2 diodes, 6 resistors and 5 supply arrows match their COCO labels (both diodes are drawn apex-down, anode on top). No unconnected leads, no dropped bridges. ERC clean.
